einzeiler: Exploring over 100 countries as a family of five with the Bucket List Family.
kurzfassung: Garrett and Jessica G share their decade-long journey of traveling the globe with their three children, starting from a modest yard-sale budget. They discuss the realities of nomadic family life, the importance of maintaining high expectations for their kids, and the lessons learned from visiting more than 90 countries. The conversation also covers their transition back to settling down in Hawaii and Jessica's new National Geographic book.
stichpunkte: Started full-time travel in 2015 after selling their belongings and generating a modest starting fund.
Traveled to over 90 countries with three young children while building a global travel brand.
Sold Garrett's tech startup Scan to Snapchat before deciding to leave traditional corporate life behind.
Emphasize minimalist packing and leveraging hotel marketing partnerships to make long-term travel affordable.
Practiced service-oriented travel, including raising funds to build a school near Delhi to combat human trafficking.
Enforce high behavioral standards for their children, teaching them to be adaptable, resilient, and brave.
Settled down in Hawaii in 2018 to establish a lasting community for their family.
Jessica published a comprehensive coffee table book detailing family travel itineraries through National Geographic.

clips.hook: An eight-year-old on a 17-hour flight watched 16 movies straight.
clips.text: The parents recount how their young son stayed awake through an entire long-haul flight simply to consume a massive amount of movies since screen time is heavily restricted at home.

clips.hook: Russian dash cam videos show real-life wildlife and rocket mishaps.
clips.text: The couple recalls living in Russia and verifying that viral internet videos featuring bizarre road incidents, stray wildlife, and sudden explosions are entirely authentic.

clips.hook: In Fiji, strangers at the airport happily take your baby so you can relax.
clips.text: The guests explain the deeply communal and child-friendly culture in Fiji, where locals eagerly assist parents and offer childcare right upon arrival.

clips.hook: Leaning back for a video and nearly bumping into a 16-foot crocodile.
clips.text: Garrett shares a tense moment from a recent jungle trip where he casually asked if a reptile was behind him while filming, only to discover a massive crocodile right in the water.

clips.hook: Training children for courage means being brave when someone is lonely.
clips.text: The couple explains that their emphasis on toughness and bravery is not about thrill-seeking stunts, but rather preparing their children to stand up against peer pressure and befriend lonely peers.

beschreibung:
This episode has been sitting in the vault for two years, and we’re finally getting to share it with you.

We’re so grateful to The Bucket List Family for joining us and for allowing us to share this never-before-seen conversation while Abby is taking time to heal and enjoy maternity leave. We talk about raising fearless kids, traveling the world as a family, their unconventional parenting philosophy, close calls with crocodiles and great white sharks, and what they’ve learned from nearly a decade of adventure together.

We hope you enjoy this special episode as much as we loved recording it. ❤️
